cards.text: Friend, Judah just lost its king, Josiah. Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, killed him at Megiddo, so the people anoint Josiah's son Jehoahaz king in his place. Jehoahaz is twenty-three years old, and the crown is ALL his.

cards.question: As king, Jehoahaz does what is right in the sight of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Pharaoh Neco steps in. He locks Jehoahaz up at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so he can't reign in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Before Pharaoh Neco locks him up, Jehoahaz reigns in Jerusalem for only three ___.
With Jehoahaz locked up at Riblah, what does Pharaoh Neco demand from Judah?

answers.text: A hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold
A thousand horses along with their chariots
Ten thousand of Judah's men for his army

cards.text: Now Pharaoh Neco picks the next king himself: Eliakim, another son of Josiah. THREE MONTHS on the job for Jehoahaz, and Egypt's already hiring his replacement!

cards.question: Pharaoh Neco makes Eliakim son of Josiah king. What does Neco do with Eliakim's name?

cards.text: Pharaoh picked the king AND wrote his name tag. Then Neco carries Jehoahaz off to Egypt.

cards.question: Jehoahaz makes it back from Egypt and reigns in Jerusalem again.

cards.text: Jehoahaz died there in Egypt. Now King Jehoiakim has to pay Pharaoh all that silver and gold, and friend, it's got to come from SOMEWHERE.

cards.question: King Jehoiakim has to pay Pharaoh Neco the silver and gold. Where does he get it?

answers.text: He taxes the people of the land
He strips the gold off the temple doors
He sells off the royal horses

cards.question: To pay Pharaoh, Jehoiakim takes silver and gold from each person in Judah according to his ___.

cards.text: Jehoiakim becomes king at twenty-five and reigns in Jerusalem eleven years. ELEVEN YEARS is forty-four of his brother's whole reigns back to back!
But his record matches his brother's word for word: "And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his fathers had done." Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, invades.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invades during Jehoiakim's reign. What does Jehoiakim do?

answers.text: He flees to Egypt for safety

cards.question: After three ___ as Nebuchadnezzar's vassal, Jehoiakim turns and ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD sends raiders against Jehoiakim to destroy Judah: Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites AND Ammonites. Friend, that's not a knock at the door, that's the whole STREET.

cards.question: The raiders come against Judah just as the LORD had spoken through His servants the ___.

cards.text: And the text says why: it happened at the LORD's command, to remove Judah from His presence because of the sins of Manasseh, an earlier king of Judah. Manasseh had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood.

cards.question: The LORD was willing to forgive the innocent blood Manasseh shed in Jerusalem.

cards.text: The rest of Jehoiakim's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, and then he rests with his fathers.

cards.question: Jehoiakim rests with his fathers. Who reigns in his place?
After all this, the king of Egypt never marches out of his land again. Why not?

answers.text: Babylon had taken all his territory
He had made peace with Judah
A plague had struck his army

cards.text: From the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates, it's Babylon's now, and Egypt is staying HOME. Keep that oven warm, friend, because Judah's story is not done yet.

findings.problem: The word "only" in "reigns in Jerusalem for only three ___" points straight to "months." Nobody says a reign lasted "only three decades," and "only three years" is a stretch. The question's own wording makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card calls Manasseh "an earlier king of Judah." That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Kings 21:1), but the card only cites 2 Kings 24:3-4, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "His brother Jehoahaz" was already ruled out in stop 1. Card 9 asks whether Jehoahaz comes back from Egypt, and card 10 then says "Jehoahaz died there in Egypt." That leaves only two real choices, so the question is easier than it should be.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
